Bely—the Docent—escaped from the colony.
445:
Unbelievable, but true. It's dangerous for you
to stay in that appearance.
446:
Maybe tomorrow? It's still New Year's,
and in their own way they tried too.
447:
We live out of town. It's unlikely
the Docent could find us.
448:
All right, but not a step off the dacha!
Also, we forwarded your letter
449:
to Sheremetyev's wife. Here's her reply.
Addressed to him.
450:
- Lunch with us on the first, promise?
- We promise!
451:
It's a pity—such a good woman, and her father
is a fence, a speculator.
452:
Why are you yelling? Who allowed you to come out?
- He showed up... A bad person.
454:
The New Year has come. I wish that in this
new year, everything for you will be new.
455:
Anything can happen, but know this:
Wherever you may be, wherever I may be,
456:
I will always remember you,
and I will find you for sure.
457:
- And now... one moment...
- Where's he off to?
458:
Who knows? With him now you can't
make out anything.
459:
What's there to make out? "Wherever you are," he says,
"I'll find you and slit your throat."
461:
They say he once took a razor to Ryaboy's throat—snip, and bye-bye.
- Totally feral, the jackal.
462:
Who's come to see you? It's Ded Moroz,
he brought you gifts!
463:
- Fedya, come here. - What did I do now?
- Come on, come on. Wear them in good health—house slippers.
464:
- What the hell do I need them for? I don't even have a home.
- You will. It's all ahead.
465:
- For now they'll be useful in prison too. Wear them.
- All you know how to do is croak.
466:
These are for you, Vasya... Gavrila Petrovich, these are for you.
- Thanks.
467:
- Pure wool.
- These are for you too.
470:
- So you have to get drunk like a pig?
- What else is there to do?
471:
We could just sit and talk
heart to heart.
472:
I'm not a prosecutor to have heart-to-heart talks with you.
- We could play a game.
473:
Would you look at that! Found yourself a sucker to play with!
You've got nine aces in the deck.
474: Why does it have to be cards?
475:
Here's a good game—cities.
I say "Moscow,"
476:
and you say a city starting with the last letter, "A"—Astrakhan.
Then you say one on "N"—Novgorod, get it?
478:
Vorkuta.
Why? I did time there.
479:
- Good. And you, then—on "A."
- Jambul. - What's Jambul got to do with it?
480:
Because it's warm there, it's my home,
it's my mom.
481:
Then let's play like this. I'll go out, you hide something,
I'll come back and find it.
482:
- You'd better find our helmet.
- Shut up.
483:
- We'll hide it, and he'll peek through a crack?
- Why? You go out and hide it.
484:
And you watch so I don't peek.
Why me? Anything happens—it's Fedya again.
485:
- And I'll rip your jaws off, you filthy little bastard!
- Jaws, jaws...
486:
- Docent, were you ever little?
- I was.
487:
- Did you have a dad and mom?
- I did.
488: Why are you so mean? Why like a dog?
490:
- Came on my own.
- Oh, so you're here too.
491:
I was about to drop by, but I can feel
there's an ambush there.
492: Mityai, I need to lie low.
494:
- Where are we going?
- Come on.
495:
- Sorry, Doctor, for bothering you for nothing.
- It's fine.
496:
Give him some valerian, warm tea, and let him sleep.
- Thank you.
497:
- Does it hurt, Garik?
- It hurts, Vasya. Read.
499:
"Hello, dear Dad! We found out that
you're in prison
500:
and we were very happy, because we thought
you were dead."
501: What bastard ratted on this little punk about Shmire?
502:
"And Mom was happy too, because
when the letter came, she cried all day,
503:
and before that she said you were
a test pilot."
505:
"And I'm happy anyway that you're alive, because
Mom says
507:
Exactly! Weak-willed—stole the communal money
and blamed the cabbie.
508: Make tracks! I'll smash your horns, you radish!
510:
Aren't you ashamed! You're 40 years old,
half your life is already gone.
511:
What's behind you? What's in the present?
What's ahead?
512:
Darkness, filth, and nothing human!
Come to your senses while it's not too late. That's my advice.
513:
Listen, Docent, we gotta blow town:
The lady doctor will tip off the police.
514:
- She won't. - Why not?
- I did her in—razor to the throat...
515: she's in the well, you can go look.
516: How much did I have? One year.
518:
How much for the kindergarten and the apartment?
Let's say ten!
519:
- How much is that total?
- Fourteen.
520: And for a lousy fourteen years I'm supposed to put up with that viper?
521:
The one the old lady put in the well?
Do what you want, I'm going to the police.
523:
And you? You'll keep tolerating him
till you die, huh?
524:
Vas, just recently I tell him: I've got
a runny nose, and he...
525:
Enough, I'm sick of your runny nose.
Come here...
526:
- Where are you here?
- Right here.
527:
- What are you up to?
- We're going to beat the rug.
528:
That's it, comrades. Finita la commedia.
First of all, I'm taking this off.
530:
I'll do my time and that's it. I'll quit!
Get a job.
531:
- As what? A watchman back on my collective farm.
- Why a watchman?
532:
I can shovel snow, lay bricks, or be
a translator—I know English.
533:
If only we'd brought the hat too!
Who's the Docent? A crook.
534:
- There are lots of crooks, but only one hat.
- If we brought in the helmet, they'd cut our time.
535: Where did he put it? We searched everywhere.
536:
Crook! Did I tell you I had a runny nose?
And you: Jaws, jaws.
537:
- Made me dive in this freezing cold!
- When did he make you dive?
538:
When they nabbed us. Remember? He says,
"I'm fishing," and you dive.
539:
- Wait—what did he say about the fish then?
- "I'm fishing in an ice hole,
540:
and you, Cross-Eyes, can you swim?"
- He hid the helmet in the ice hole—that's what!
541:
Exactly! I remember, bad person!
In the ice hole—in Malakhovka!
542:
Why didn't you say so, you lout? You could've left a note when you hanged yourself.
- Let's go.
543:
- And him?
- Forget him. Let them pick him up themselves. Carrying a hog like that. Let's go!
545:
- There's jack shit there.
- It's there, on the bottom. Someone has to dive.
546:
Why me? Anything happens—it's Cross-Eyes.
Vas, tell him to go in himself.
547: I can't! It's cold, I'll get sick.
548:
- Just tried to hang himself, now he's afraid of catching cold!
- Physical-culture greetings!
550:
- Where's the boat station?
- Over there.
551: I'd stitch you up, but I haven't got time to mess around!
552:
Now that's two of them.
And one more back at the dacha.
554:
- One!
- Well done, Fyodor Petrovich, well done!
555:
- Two.
- The more we turn in, the better.
